# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 67 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 67 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_067_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 6, Part 5 — Types of Sinners and Their Punishments

**67:1** "Why, lord," I said, "are there some servants of God who always live well and do not sin, and yet receive so many torments and adversities in their lives?" "How long," he said, "will you be without understanding? You always ask questions about everything. You are too persistent."

**67:2** "Listen," he said. "Those who seem to always do good and not to sin — these are not to be thought of as having no sin. But they sin each day, though with small sins. They sin in speech and in action and even in thought. And because their sins are small, the Lord does not punish them greatly, but torments them in lesser ways."

**67:3** "But those who have great and accumulated sins receive greater torments, for they are handed over to the angel of punishment for a long time." "Nevertheless, lord," I said, "if any have sinned greatly and are being punished — will they eventually be saved?" "Yes," he said, "but their salvation is delayed."

**67:4** I said to him: "Lord, I wish to know the nature of the various torments and afflictions. Are they of different kinds?" "They are," he said. "And I will show you which kinds apply to which persons.

**67:5** The torments and afflictions that come upon men in this life are these: losses, and wanderings, and various illnesses, and disturbances of every sort, and separations of friends and of those we love, and poverty, and every other trouble. For these are the torments that the servants of God must go through in their lives, for the Lord, who is rich in mercy, chastises them so that they may be purified."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the taxonomy of punishments in Similitude 6.*
